The Babylonian system is positional with base 60.
1. Split the cuneiform by place-value: 𒐜 (left) and 𒐐𒐚 (right).
2. Convert each group to its decimal value:
   • 𒐜 = 8.
   • 𒐐 = 5 and 𒐚 = 6; together in the same place-value position they sum: 5 + 6 = 11 (still < 60, so valid as one sexagesimal digit).
3. Evaluate the sexagesimal number 8 | 11 → 8×60 + 11 = 480 + 11 = 491.
Mesopotamian numbers are written in base 60, with each space-separated cluster being one sexagesimal digit.

1. Identify the two sexagesimal digits
   • 𒐜  → value 8
   • 𒐐𒐚 → 𒐐 (5) + 𒐚 (6) = 11

2. Convert to decimal
   (8 × 60¹) + (11 × 60⁰) = 480 + 11 = 491
